s: Which Act replaced the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act (FERA), 1973?
x: FERA 1973 was replaced by FEMA 1999.

s: The New Industrial Policy, 1991 was introduced in the context of which major economic difficulty?
x: The 1991 policy was introduced after India faced a severe balance-of-payments crisis.

s: The New Industrial Policy, 1991 was announced when P. V. Narasimha Rao was Prime Minister. Which post did Manmohan Singh then hold?
x: The 1991 policy was announced by Prime Minister P. V. Narasimha Rao, with Manmohan Singh as Finance Minister.

s: After later reductions, compulsory industrial licensing under the New Industrial Policy, 1991 continues for how many industries?
x:
The printed options did not include the correct answer (4); it is added as option 5.
alcohol dropped out of the licensing list — now 4 industries (DPIIT Press Note 3, 2019)
DPIIT's Press Note 3 (2019) leaves only four industries under compulsory licensing: cigars and cigarettes, electronic aerospace and defence equipment, industrial explosives and hazardous chemicals. 'Five' (with alcohol) is the older count.

s: Which of the following industries was later delicensed and is no longer under compulsory industrial licensing?
x:
Most books: alcohol is still licensed (five industries). Strictly: DPIIT Press Note 3 (2019) lists only four, without alcohol.
Drugs and pharmaceuticals were in the older six-item list and were later delicensed. Hazardous chemicals and industrial explosives are still licensed. Alcohol, which older books list among the five, also no longer appears in DPIIT's 2019 list of four.

s: What was an industrial unit delicensed under the New Industrial Policy, 1991 required to file?
o: A Foreign Investment Promotion Board application
x: Delicensed units were required to file only an Industrial Entrepreneur Memorandum (IEM).

s: Which of the following was a major effect of the 1991 industrial reforms?
o: Replacement of private industry by exclusive state ownership
Continuation of all expansion limits and price controls
Removal of licensing, expansion limits, price controls and import-export restrictions
x: The 1991 reforms ended the licence-permit-quota raj by removing industrial licensing, expansion limits, price controls and import-export restrictions.

s: Of which of the following was the New Industrial Policy of 1991 the primary starting anchor?
x: The New Industrial Policy of 24 July 1991 was the starting point of liberalisation. It ended licensing for most industries.

s: What major shift in the role of government took place after the 1991 reforms?
x: The reforms shifted the government’s role from direct regulation towards facilitation, forming the basis for today’s FDI framework and competition law.

s: Which of the following was delicensed in 1993 under the New Industrial Policy reforms?
x: Automobiles, white goods and leather were delicensed in 1993. Industrial explosives and hazardous chemicals are still licensed (alcohol is no longer on DPIIT's 2019 list).

s:
Assertion (A): Liberalisation instruments boost domestic manufacturing competitiveness.
Reason (R): They lower the cost of technology and capital equipment.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both are true: liberalisation tools such as lower import duties make domestic manufacturing more competitive because they cut the cost of technology and capital equipment. R explains A.

s: The beginning of the ‘licence-permit-quota raj’ in India is generally associated with which policy resolution?
x: The Industrial Policy Resolution, 1956 is associated with the beginning of the licence-permit-quota raj.

s: Which industrial policy is called the 'Bible of State Capitalism'?
x: IPR 1956 was called both the 'Economic Constitution of India' and the 'Bible of State Capitalism'.

s: At which Congress session was the socialist pattern of society adopted as the goal of economic policy?
x: The socialist pattern of society was adopted as the goal at the Avadi session in 1955.

s: Schedule A of the Industrial Policy Resolution, 1956, reserved for the State, contained how many industries?
x: Schedule A had 17 basic or strategic industries under the exclusive responsibility of the State.

s: Schedule B of the Industrial Policy Resolution, 1956 contained how many industries?
x: Schedule B had 12 industries to be progressively State-owned, with the private sector supplementing State effort.

s: Which of the following was a feature of the Industrial Policy Resolution, 1956?
x: IPR 1956 provided for licensing, public-sector expansion, small and cottage industries, balanced regional development and labour welfare. DICs came under the 1977 policy.

s: Which industrial policy formed the basis of the Second Five-Year Plan?
x: The IPR 1956, built on the Mahalanobis model of heavy and basic industries, formed the basis of the Second Plan. IPR 1948 came before the First Plan; the 1977 Statement stressed small and cottage industries and DICs; the 1980 Statement stressed economic federalism and exports.

s: Which of the following explains the significance of the Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956?
o: Established the public-sector-led, licence-based industrial model that continued until 1991
Introduced complete deregulation of all industries
Ended the role of the public sector in basic industries
Restricted industrial development entirely to foreign companies
x: The 1956 Resolution shaped a public-sector-led and licence-based industrial model that continued until the 1991 reforms.

s: Under the Industrial Policy Resolution, 1956, how were the industries in Schedule C treated?
o: Placed under joint ownership of the Centre and States
Left to private initiative subject to licensing
x: Schedule C covered all remaining industries and left them to private initiative under an industrial licensing system.

s: Who placed the Industrial Policy Resolution, 1956 before Parliament?
x: IPR 1956, announced on 30 April 1956, was placed before Parliament by Nehru.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Industrial Policy Resolution, 1956:
1. Schedule A contained 17 industries.
2. Schedule B contained 12 industries.
3. Its licensing rested on the MRTP Act, 1969.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Schedule A had 17 and Schedule B 12 industries; licensing rested on the IDR Act, 1951, not the MRTP Act.

s: The Second Five-Year Plan, based on IPR 1956, followed which model of heavy and basic industries?
x: IPR 1956 was the basis of the Second Plan, which followed the Mahalanobis model of heavy and basic industries.

s: Under the Industrial Policy Resolution, 1956, in which schedule was aluminium placed?
o: It was kept outside all schedules
x: Schedule B (12 industries) included aluminium, machine tools, ferro-alloys and basic chemicals.

s: Who announced the Industrial Policy Resolution of 1948?
x: The 1948 Resolution was announced by Industry Minister Dr. Shyama Prasad Mukherjee.

s: The Industrial Policy Resolution, 1948 laid the foundation for which economic system in India?
x: The 1948 Resolution defined roles for both the public and private sectors and thereby laid the foundation of a mixed economy.

s: Under the Industrial Policy Resolution, 1948, in which category was shipbuilding placed?
x: Coal, mineral oils, iron and steel, aircraft, shipbuilding and telephone/telegraph apparatus formed the six mixed-sector industries.

s: Under the Industrial Policy Resolution, 1948, which group was placed under exclusive Central monopoly?
o: Coal, iron and steel, and cement
Arms and ammunition, atomic energy, and railways
x: Arms and ammunition, atomic energy and railways were placed under exclusive Central monopoly in the 1948 policy.

s: How many industries were placed in the mixed sector under the Industrial Policy Resolution, 1948?
x: IPR 1948 placed 6 industries (coal, mineral oils, iron and steel, aircraft, shipbuilding, telephone apparatus) in the mixed sector.

s: Under IPR 1948, existing private units in the mixed sector were allowed to continue for how many years before review?
x: New units in the mixed sector were for the State; existing private units got 10 years, then review.

s: Which of the following was NOT under exclusive Central monopoly in the Industrial Policy Resolution, 1948?
x: Iron and steel was in the mixed sector; arms, atomic energy and railways were Central monopolies.

s: Which was the first industrial policy of independent India?
x: The IPR of 6 April 1948 was the first; the 1945 statement came before independence.

s: Under the Industrial Policy Resolution, 1948, how many industries were placed in the centrally regulated category?
x: IPR 1948 put 18 industries (salt, automobiles, cement, sugar, textiles etc.) under Central regulation; 6 were in the mixed sector.

s: What did the mandatory convertibility clause in the 1991 industrial policy framework concern?
o: Rupee convertibility on the current account
Conversion of foreign equity into domestic equity
Conversion of PSUs into joint-stock companies
Financial institutions converting term loans into equity
x: The clause allowed financial institutions to convert their term loans to a company into equity. The 1991 policy abolished this mandatory clause for term loans of new projects, freeing firms from the threat of State takeover.

s: Which body was established under the New Industrial Policy, 1991 to speed up foreign investment approvals?
o: Board for Industrial and Financial Reconstruction
Department of Investment and Public Asset Management
x: The FIPB was set up as part of the liberalised foreign investment framework of the 1991 policy.

s: When was the Foreign Investment Promotion Board (FIPB) abolished?
x: FIPB was abolished in June 2017 and approvals moved to the FIF portal.

s: Why did mergers and acquisitions become easier after the 1991 reforms?
o: Prior approval under the MRTP framework was removed
x: Removal of MRTP pre-approval for mergers and acquisitions directly made them easier after 1991.

s: Under the New Industrial Policy, 1991, for which of the following was automatic approval also given?
o: Foreign technology agreements in priority industries
FDI in all industries without limit
x: NIP 1991 gave automatic approval for foreign technology agreements in priority industries and allowed foreign brand names.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about foreign investment under the New Industrial Policy, 1991?
o: Automatic approval up to 51% applied to all industries
FIPB was set up to speed approvals
Equity in SSI units by others was allowed up to 24%
x: Automatic approval up to 51% applied only to a list of high-priority industries, not all industries.

s: What was the MRTP-related change made by the New Industrial Policy, 1991?
o: Raising the asset threshold to Rs 1,000 crore
x: NIP 1991 scrapped the MRTP asset threshold, removing prior approval for expansion and mergers.

s: After the FIPB was abolished in 2017, which platform was launched in August 2022 for investment approvals?
x: FIPB gave way to the FIF portal, which merged into the National Single Window System in August 2022.

s: The R. K. Hazari report of 1967 primarily examined which subject?
x: The R. K. Hazari report examined industrial licensing and reported that big business houses had cornered licences.

s: Which of the following was a criticism of the licence raj?
o: It produced excess scale in firms
x: The licence raj was criticised for rent-seeking, entry barriers and keeping firms from adequate scale, not for excess scale.

s: Which Act was enacted as a result of the Industrial Licensing Policy Inquiry Committee (Dutt Committee) report of 1969?
x: The Subimal Dutt Committee report (1969) led to the MRTP Act.

s: The 'joint sector' concept was set out by which committee?
x: The joint sector (State + private partnership) was set out by the Dutt Committee (1969); IPR 1948 had created the mixed sector.

s: What did the R.K. Hazari report (1967) find about industrial licensing?
o: Big business houses had cornered the licences
Public sector units were refused licences
x: The Hazari report found that big business houses had cornered industrial licences.

s: Which law replaced the MRTP Act?
x: The MRTP Act was replaced by the Competition Act, 2002, after the 1991 policy scrapped the MRTP asset threshold.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Industrial Policy Statement, 1977 – Core sector list
Industrial Policy Statement, 1977 – District Industries Centres
Industrial Policy Statement, 1980 – District Industries Centres
x: District Industries Centres came with the 1977 policy; the 1973 Statement gave the core sector list and economic federalism belongs to 1980.

s: The Industrial Policy Statement of which year first gave strong emphasis to exports?
x: The 1980 Statement was the first to give strong emphasis to export orientation.

s: Who largely drafted the Industrial Policy Statement of 1977?
x: The Janata Government's 1977 Statement was largely drafted by George Fernandes, not Morarji Desai.

s: For what purpose were District Industries Centres (1977) mainly set up?
o: Grant licences to large industrial houses
Provide one-roof support to small and cottage industries in each district
x: DICs were established in every district to give integrated, one-roof support to small and cottage industries.

s: In which year did reservation of items for the small-scale sector begin in India?
x: SSI item reservation began in 1967, not after the New Industrial Policy, 1991.

s:
Consider the following about the Industrial Policy Statement, 1980:
1. It emphasised technological upgradation and modernisation.
2. It gave strong emphasis to export orientation.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
x: The 1980 policy stressed technological upgradation and modernisation, with export orientation strongly emphasised for the first time.

s: 'Economic federalism' in the Industrial Policy Statement, 1980 meant incentives such as tax holidays and cheap credit for which of the following?
x: Economic federalism meant targeted incentives, such as tax holidays and cheap credit, for backward districts, not uniform incentives.

s: Through which of the following did the Industrial Policy Statement of 1977 mainly curb large industrial houses?
x: The policy used the MRTP and FERA frameworks to curb the influence of large industrial houses.

s: Which multinational companies left India after the 1977 policy curbed large houses through MRTP and FERA?
x: The 1977 policy curbed large houses through MRTP and FERA, after which IBM and Coca-Cola left India.

s: Under the Industrial Policy Statement, 1980, by up to what share could MRTP firms expand capacity without approval?
x: The 1980 Statement let MRTP firms expand capacity by 25% without approval.

s: In which year was reservation of items for small-scale industries fully removed?
x: SSI reservation began in 1967, continued after 1991 and was fully dereserved in 2015.

s: Under the Industrial Policy Statement of which year were District Industries Centres created?
x: DICs were created under the 1977 policy; the 1973 Statement identified a core-sector list and tightened MRTP.

s: Which industrial policy emphasised 'tiny' units, khadi and handlooms, and employment generation?
x: The 1977 Statement emphasised small-scale and tiny units, khadi and handlooms, and employment generation.

s: Which industrial policy statement first identified a list of 'core sector' industries?
x: The 1973 statement drew up a core sector list and tightened MRTP.

s: The MSME and Entrepreneur Development Policy 4.0 (2024-29) provides for how many MSME parks?
x: Policy 4.0 provides for 175 MSME parks, 'One Family One Entrepreneur' by 2030 and capital subsidy of 25% (45% for special categories).

s: Under Andhra Pradesh Industrial Development Policy 4.0 (2024-29), which of the following is classified as a 'propelling' sector rather than a 'sustenance' sector?
x: Propelling sectors are semiconductors and electronics, EVs, aerospace-defence, blue economy and green energy. Automobiles, pharmaceuticals and textiles (with chemicals) are sustenance sectors.

s: Which of the following is NOT a target of Andhra Pradesh Industrial Development Policy 4.0?
x: The targets include ₹30 lakh crore investment, USD 10 billion FDI and five lakh manufacturing jobs; USD 100 billion FDI is not specified.

s: Which authority chairs the State Investment Promotion Board (SIPB) in Andhra Pradesh?
x: The SIPB is chaired by the Chief Minister, while the SIPC is associated with the Chief Secretary.

s: What is the target for industrial parks and exports under Industrial Development Policy (4.0) 2024-29?
o: 200 industrial parks and increase exports from US$10 billion to US$30 billion
40+ industrial parks and increase exports from US$20 billion to US$175 billion
175+ industrial parks and increase exports from US$20 billion to US$40 billion
175+ industrial parks and increase exports from US$40 billion to US$20 billion
x: The policy targets more than 175 industrial parks and an increase in exports from US$20 billion to US$40 billion.

s: What does the MSME and Entrepreneur Development Policy 4.0 of Andhra Pradesh aim at?
x: The MSME Policy 4.0 aims at 'One Family One Entrepreneur' by 2030.

s: Which is the nodal agency of the Andhra Pradesh Maritime Policy 2024-29?
x: The AP Maritime Board is the nodal agency of the Maritime Policy 2024-29.

s: Who chairs the State Investment Promotion Committee (SIPC) in Andhra Pradesh?
x: SIPB is chaired by the Chief Minister and SIPC by the Chief Secretary.

s: What is the FDI target of Andhra Pradesh Industrial Development Policy 4.0 (2024-29)?
x: The FDI target is USD 10 bn, not 100 bn.

s: For how long is the Andhra Pradesh Industrial Development Policy 4.0 valid?
o: Five years or till a new policy is notified
x: Policy 4.0 (G.O.Ms.No.68, 26 Oct 2024) is valid for five years (2024-29) or till a new policy.

s: What capital subsidy does the Andhra Pradesh MSME and Entrepreneur Development Policy 4.0 give to general MSMEs?
x: The policy gives a 25% capital subsidy, rising to 45% for special categories.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Andhra Pradesh Maritime Policy 2024-29:
1. It aims to have one AP port among the world's top 20 by 2047.
2. Its nodal agency is APIIC.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The policy aims at a top-20 world port by 2047; its nodal agency is the AP Maritime Board, not APIIC.

s: What share of India's port cargo does the Andhra Pradesh Maritime Policy 2024-29 aim to handle?
x: The policy aims for AP to handle 20% of India's port cargo.

s: What is the period of Andhra Pradesh's Aerospace and Defence Policy 4.0?
x: The Aerospace and Defence and Space 4.0 policies cover 2025-30; most other 4.0 policies cover 2024-29.

s: Which industry was NOT on the public-sector-only list of the New Industrial Policy, 1991 as originally framed?
x: Defence equipment, atomic energy and railway transport were on the public-sector-only list; pharmaceuticals were never reserved for the public sector.

s: Under the New Industrial Policy, 1991, through what was autonomy granted to public-sector undertakings?
x: The 1991 policy granted PSU autonomy through MoUs, referred sick PSUs to BIFR and began disinvestment in 1991-92.

s: How many industries were reserved for the public sector under the New Industrial Policy, 1991?
x: Eight industries were reserved in 1991; this was cut to three and, after May 2001, to two (atomic energy and railway operations).

s: In which year was SICA repealed and BIFR dissolved, with cases moving under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code?
x: SICA was repealed and BIFR dissolved in 2016; pending cases moved under the IBC.

s: How many industries are reserved for the public sector at present?
x: Reservation fell 17 to 8 to 3 to 2; atomic energy and railway operations remain.

s: Which two industries remain reserved for the public sector today?
o: Arms and ammunition and railway operations
x: Today only atomic energy and railway operations are reserved; arms and ammunition were opened on 9 May 2001.

s: Under the 1991 PSU measures, to which body were chronically sick public sector units referred?
x: Chronically sick PSUs were referred to BIFR under SICA 1985.

s: Disinvestment of up to what share in selected PSUs began in 1991-92?
x: The 1991 measures provided for up to 20% disinvestment in selected PSUs, beginning 1991-92.

s: In which year was the National Renewal Fund set up?
x: The National Renewal Fund was set up in 1992 under the 1991 PSU measures to help displaced workers.

s: In which year were arms and ammunition opened to the private sector?
x: Arms and ammunition were opened to the private sector on 9 May 2001.

s: A criticism of the post-1991 industrial policy is that investment became concentrated in which States?
o: Maharashtra, Gujarat, Tamil Nadu and Karnataka
Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh
Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Odisha and Assam
Kerala, West Bengal, Jharkhand and Bihar
x: Investment concentrated in Maharashtra, Gujarat, Tamil Nadu and Karnataka, making regional imbalance a criticism.

s: Which one of the following was NOT a criticism of the 1991 industrial policy?
x: Increase in consumer choice was an achievement associated with the post-1991 reforms, not a criticism. The other three were criticisms.

s: After 1991, what adversely affected many small-scale units?
o: A ban on imports of capital goods
Import competition following removal of protection
x: Removal of protection exposed small units to import competition, which hurt many of them; SSI reservation continued after 1991.

s: When did India's forex reserves touch a record of about USD 702.28 billion?
x: Forex reserves reached a record USD 702.28 bn in November 2025.

s: Which department has the mandate to formulate India's FDI policy?
x: DPIIT's mandate includes FDI policy, Startups, industrial corridors and IPR matters.

s: In which year was DIPP renamed the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT)?
x: DIPP became DPIIT in 2019, adding internal trade, traders' welfare and Startups; logistics was allotted only in November 2021.

s: In which year was the Department of Industrial Policy and Promotion (DIPP) created as a separate department?
x: DIPP was created as a separate department in 1995. 1961 is when the Department of Industry was set up, 1967 is when it was renamed the Department of Industrial Development, and 2019 is when DIPP was renamed DPIIT.

s: What is the full form of DPIIT?
o: Department of Policy for Industry and International Trade
Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade
Department of Promotion of Industrial Investment and Trade
Department for Planning of Industry and Internal Trade
x: DIPP was renamed the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade in 2019.

s: When was the logistics mandate allotted to DPIIT?
x: DPIIT received the logistics mandate in November 2021.

s:
Arrange the following enactments in chronological order:
A. Sick Industrial Companies Act
B. MRTP Act
C. Industries (Development and Regulation) Act
D. FERA
x: The correct order is Industries (Development and Regulation) Act, 1951; MRTP Act, 1969; FERA, 1973; and Sick Industrial Companies Act, 1985.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: 1956 – IDR Act establishing the licensing framework
1951 – Industrial Policy Resolution with public-sector dominance
x: The SEZ Policy came in 2000; the IDR Act is of 1951, the public-sector-led Resolution of 1956 and the New Industrial Policy of 1991.

s: When was the Special Economic Zone (SEZ) Policy of India announced?
x: The SEZ Policy was announced on 1 April 2000 to attract investment and promote exports; 24 July 1991 is the New Industrial Policy.

s: Under the original SICA, 1985, for at least how many years must a sick industrial company have been registered?
x: The original definition required at least seven years of registration, accumulated losses equal to or exceeding net worth, and cash losses.

s: Which change was introduced by the 1993 amendment to the SICA definition of a sick company?
o: The registration requirement was increased to ten years and cash losses were retained.
The registration requirement was reduced to three years and net worth was excluded.
The registration requirement was abolished and accumulated losses were ignored.
The registration requirement was reduced to five years and the cash-loss test was dropped.
x: The 1993 amendment reduced the minimum registration period from seven to five years and dropped the cash-loss test.

s: Under RBI norms, a micro or small unit is sick if any of its borrowal accounts stays NPA for more than how long?
x: An NPA lasting more than 3 months marks a micro or small unit as sick (with 50% net-worth erosion as the other test).

s: Under RBI norms, a micro or small unit is also sick if its net worth is eroded by how much?
x: RBI treats a micro or small unit as sick on NPA over 3 months or 50% net-worth erosion.

s: Under the RBI framework of 2016, how is early stress in a loan account classified?
x: The RBI 2016 framework tags early stress as Special Mention Accounts SMA-0, SMA-1 and SMA-2.

s: Under the original SICA, 1985, which condition made a company sick?
o: Accumulated losses equal to or more than its net worth
A fall of 50% in net profit
An NPA account for three months
x: SICA 1985 treated a company (registered 7+ years) as sick if accumulated losses equalled or exceeded its net worth.

s: How is obsolete technology classified as a cause of industrial sickness?
x: Obsolete technology is an internal production cause; poor working-capital management is internal finance, competition external demand, EXIM changes external policy.

s: Which of the following is an external cause of industrial sickness?
x: Power shortage is external; the other three are internal management failures.

s: Which of the following is NOT an internal cause of industrial sickness?
x: Sudden EXIM, tax or environment policy changes are external causes.

s: Which of the following is a major trigger of sickness among MSMEs?
o: Delayed payments by large buyers and government
x: Delayed payments by large buyers and government are a major trigger of MSME sickness.

s: Which of the following is NOT a consequence of industrial sickness?
o: Bank loans turning into non-performing assets
Plant, land and funds lying idle
Increase in revenue receipts of the exchequer
x: Idle assets in sick units cause revenue loss to the exchequer, not an increase; NPAs, locked capital and unemployment are real consequences.

s: Why did the State take over certain sick private textile and engineering units?
o: Earn dividend income for the State
x: The State took over certain sick private units, especially in textiles and engineering, mainly to protect jobs.

s: Industrial sickness has been particularly concentrated in which group of sectors?
x: The sectors especially associated with industrial sickness are textiles, including cotton mills, jute, sugar and engineering.

s: Which of the following is a consequence of industrial sickness?
x: Sickness causes NPAs, locked capital, unemployment and revenue loss, not higher revenue.

s: Which of the following sectors is NOT among those with the most sick units?
x: Sickness has been concentrated in textiles, jute, sugar and engineering.

s: In which year was the Sick Industrial Companies (Special Provisions) Act (SICA) enacted?
x: SICA was enacted in 1985 following the Tiwari Committee (1984-85); BIFR was set up in January 1987.

s: Which institution, set up in 1971, was associated with the rehabilitation of sick industrial units?
o: Appellate Authority for Industrial and Financial Reconstruction
x: The Industrial Reconstruction Corporation of India (IRCI), set up in 1971, was the first institution for rehabilitating sick industrial units. It became the Industrial Reconstruction Bank of India (IRBI) in 1985.

s: With what was the Board for Industrial and Financial Reconstruction (BIFR) concerned?
o: Refinancing banks that lend to small industries
Early detection of sickness, revival of viable units and closure of unviable units
x: BIFR dealt with early detection of industrial sickness, revival of viable units and winding-up of unviable units.

s: When was the Board for Industrial and Financial Reconstruction (BIFR) set up?
x: BIFR was set up in January 1987, after SICA 1985.

s: With which body did appeals against BIFR orders lie?
x: Appeals from BIFR went to the AAIFR.

s: On the recommendation of which committee was SICA, 1985 enacted?
x: The Tiwari Committee (1984-85) led to SICA 1985 and the BIFR.

s: In 1985, the Industrial Reconstruction Corporation of India (IRCI) was converted into which body?
x: IRCI (1971), the first rehabilitation institution, became the Industrial Reconstruction Bank of India (IRBI) in 1985.

s: Under which Ministry did the Board for Industrial and Financial Reconstruction (BIFR) function?
x: BIFR came under the Department of Financial Services, Ministry of Finance.

s: Under the new insolvency regime, which body succeeded the BIFR?
x: BIFR was succeeded by the NCLT and AAIFR by the NCLAT; SICA's regime was replaced by the IBC, 2016.

s:
Consider the following statements about the shift from SICA to the IBC:
1. It strengthened the position of creditors in insolvency resolution.
2. The earlier SICA framework was criticised for protecting defaulting promoters.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both are true: SICA protected defaulting promoters and let BIFR proceedings drag on, and the IBC gave creditors a stronger role.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched under the IBC framework?
x: Under the IBC the NCLT is the adjudicating authority; NCLAT is the appellate tribunal and IBBI is the regulator.

s:
Consider the following statements about the failure of the BIFR-based regime:
1. It suffered from procedural delays.
2. It resolved sick units too rapidly.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The regime failed due to procedural delays, legal loopholes and weak revival; rapid resolution was not a reason.

s: Under the IBC framework, which body is the successor of the AAIFR?
x: BIFR was succeeded by NCLT and AAIFR by NCLAT.

s: When were BIFR and AAIFR dissolved?
x: BIFR and AAIFR were dissolved on 1 December 2016.

s: Which committee examined insolvency and winding-up, leading to the NCLT and NCLAT?
x: The Eradi Committee led to NCLT/NCLAT; Tiwari led to SICA and BIFR, Goswami studied corporate restructuring, Kohli sick SSI units.

s: Which committee's recommendations formed the basis of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016?
x: The IBC was based on the T.K. Viswanathan Committee, also known as the Bankruptcy Law Reforms Committee, 2015.

s: Which committee examined sick SSI units in 1999-2000?
x: The Kohli Committee (1999-2000) dealt with sick SSI units.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Omkar Goswami Committee – Sickness and corporate restructuring
x: Omkar Goswami (1993) dealt with sickness and corporate restructuring; Tiwari led to SICA, Eradi to NCLT/NCLAT, Kohli to sick SSI units.

s: A one-time restructuring of stressed MSME loans without asset-classification downgrade was permitted in which year (later extended during 2020-21)?
x: The one-time restructuring of stressed MSME loans without downgrade was permitted in 2019 and extended during 2020-21.

s: What was the principal purpose of the National Renewal Fund?
o: Finance voluntary retirement, retraining and redeployment of displaced workers
Provide foreign exchange to importing firms
x: The Fund financed voluntary retirement schemes, retraining and redeployment for workers displaced by restructuring or closure of industrial units.

s: At present, through which mechanism are delayed payments to MSMEs addressed?
x: MSME Samadhaan handles delayed payments, while company insolvency goes to NCLT under the IBC, 2016.

s: To tackle delayed payments to MSMEs, through which platform did the MSME Bill passed by the Rajya Sabha in August 2026 require CPSEs to settle MSME invoices?
x: The measure required Central Public Sector Enterprises to settle MSME invoices through the Trade Receivables Discounting System (TReDS).

s: Which scheme of June 1987 helped reduce sickness in small-scale units?
x: The Liberalised Margin Money Scheme (June 1987) reduced SSI sickness.

s: In which year was the National Renewal Fund wound up?
x: The NRF was set up in 1992 and wound up in 2000.

s: What is the sale of government equity in public sector enterprises known as?
x: Selling government equity is disinvestment; liberalisation is removal of licences, quotas and controls.

s: Which of the following correctly distinguishes disinvestment from privatisation?
o: Disinvestment always transfers management control; privatisation may retain government control
Both always transfer management control to the private sector
Disinvestment reduces government equity; privatisation transfers ownership and management control to the private sector
Privatisation reduces equity without transfer of control; disinvestment transfers ownership
x: Disinvestment is a reduction of government equity, possibly with government retaining control; privatisation transfers ownership and management control to the private sector.

s: A government retains more than 51 per cent equity and control in a public sector enterprise while selling a part of its holding. What is this called?
x: Under minority disinvestment, the government retains more than 51 per cent ownership and control. Majority disinvestment transfers control while retaining a minority stake.

s: What does a strategic sale of a public sector enterprise generally involve?
o: Sale of a block of shares, usually 50% or more, with transfer of management control
Sale of a minority stake with the government retaining control
Leasing assets for a fixed period with ownership retained by the government
Listing shares through an IPO without any change in management
x: A strategic sale normally involves a block of shares, usually 50% or more, along with transfer of management control to a strategic partner.

s: Which of the following is NOT identified as a criticism or concern relating to disinvestment?
o: Automatic improvement in public ownership of strategic assets
National-security concerns in oil, defence and transport
x: The identified concerns include undervaluation, loss of dividend income and national-security risks in sectors such as oil, defence and transport. Automatic improvement in public ownership is not a criticism of disinvestment.

s: Why is the expression “selling the family silver” used in criticism of disinvestment?
o: all public assets are sold below their book value in every transaction
the proceeds are used to bridge the fiscal deficit instead of building assets
disinvestment necessarily increases dividend income for the government
the proceeds are exclusively invested in new public enterprises
x: The expression criticises the use of disinvestment proceeds to bridge the fiscal deficit rather than to create or build assets.

s: Which mode is considered the most comprehensive mode of privatisation?
x: Complete privatisation, selling 100%, is the most comprehensive mode.

s: What is the removal of licences, quotas and controls without any sale of government equity called?
x: Liberalisation removes licences, quotas and controls; it involves no sale.

s: Which of the following is a disinvestment instrument used by DIPAM?
x: CPSE ETF, Offer for Sale, IPO/FPO and strategic sale are disinvestment instruments; SLR, CRR and repo are monetary and banking tools.

s: Which of the following is NOT a disinvestment method used by DIPAM?
x: SLR, CRR and repo are monetary tools, not disinvestment methods.

s:
Consider the following statements about the rationale of disinvestment in India:
1. It aims to reduce the fiscal deficit.
2. It seeks to improve the efficiency of PSUs.
3. It seeks to raise the share of government equity in CPSEs.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Disinvestment cuts the fiscal deficit and improves PSU efficiency; it reduces, not raises, government equity.

s: To whom was Air India sold by strategic sale in 2021-22?
x: Air India was sold to the Tata Group. Sterlite (Vedanta) bought BALCO, Hindustan Lever bought Modern Food Industries, and PFC acquired REC.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: NINL – Proceeds credited to the exchequer
x: PFC acquired REC for Rs 14,500 crore in 2018-19. The LIC IPO was in 2022, the BPCL sale was called off and NINL yielded no proceeds to the exchequer.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Modern Food Industries was sold to Hindustan Lever. BALCO was sold to Sterlite, VSNL to the Tata group and Air India to Tata Group.

s: To whom was BALCO sold by strategic sale in 2001?
x: BALCO went to Sterlite (Vedanta); VSNL and Air India went to Tata.

s: Which proposed strategic sale was called off in mid-2022?
x: The BPCL (52.8%) sale was called off in mid-2022.

s: Which company acquired the government's stake in REC in 2018-19?
x: REC was sold to PFC for Rs 14,500 crore.

s:
Match the following:
List-I (PSU sold)
a. VSNL
b. BALCO
c. HPCL
d. REC
List-II (Buyer)
1. ONGC
2. PFC
3. Tata group
4. Sterlite (Vedanta)
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: VSNL went to Tata, BALCO to Sterlite, HPCL to ONGC and REC to PFC.

s: Who founded Air India as Tata Airlines in 1932?
x: J.R.D. Tata founded Tata Airlines in 1932; it later became Air India.

s: Which company acquired Neelachal Ispat Nigam Limited (NINL) through strategic sale?
x: NINL was sold to Tata Steel; the sale brought no proceeds to the exchequer.

s: In which year was the LIC IPO, then India's biggest IPO, listed?
x: The LIC IPO listed on 17 May 2022 and was the biggest IPO at the time.

s: Which of the following is a criticism of disinvestment?
x: Disinvestment is criticised for undervaluation, lost dividends, security risks and 'selling the family silver'.

s: The Competition Act, 2002 was recommended by which committee?
x: The Competition Act, 2002 was recommended by the S.V.S. Raghavan Committee in 2000.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
x: The Competition Act was enacted in 2002 and commenced on 31 March 2003. The other pairs are correctly matched.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Competition Commission of India:
1. It functions under the Ministry of Corporate Affairs.
2. It consists of a Chairperson and two to six members.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both are true: the CCI, set up on 14 October 2003, is under the Ministry of Corporate Affairs and has a Chairperson and 2-6 members.

s: Under the Competition Act, 2002, which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Cartels, bid-rigging and price-fixing are anti-competitive agreements under Section 3; unfair pricing and denial of market access are abuse of dominance (Section 4), and M&A above thresholds are combinations (Sections 5-6).

s: If the CCI does not decide on a combination within the prescribed deadline, what happens to the combination?
x: A combination is deemed approved if the CCI misses the prescribed decision deadline.

s: Which section of the Competition Act, 2002 deals with abuse of dominance?
x: Section 4 covers abuse of dominance; Section 3 covers anti-competitive agreements.

s: Which body hears appeals against orders of the CCI?
x: NCLAT has heard CCI appeals since 26 May 2017.

s: Who became the Chairperson of the Competition Commission of India in May 2023?
x: Ravneet Kaur became CCI Chairperson in May 2023; Ashok Chawla was an earlier chairperson.

s: When did the anti-competitive provisions of the Competition Act, 2002 come into force?
x: Anti-competitive provisions came into force on 20 May 2009; merger control began in June 2011.

s: How much penalty did the Competition Commission of India impose on Google in 2022?
x: CCI fined Google ₹1,337 crore in 2022 for abuse of dominance (Android).

s: On which company did the Competition Commission of India impose a penalty of ₹213.14 crore in 2024?
x: CCI fined Meta ₹213.14 crore (2024) over WhatsApp's privacy policy; NCLAT upheld the fine in 2025.

s: From when did merger (combination) control under the Competition Act, 2002 come into force?
x: Anti-competitive provisions came into force on 20 May 2009 and combination control from June 2011.

s: Up to what share did the Rangarajan Committee (1993) recommend disinvestment in PSUs reserved for the public sector?
x: It recommended disinvestment up to 49% in PSUs reserved for the public sector and up to 74% in other enterprises.

s: Under which Ministry does DIPAM, which manages Central Government equity and disinvestment, function?
x: DIPAM (renamed from the Department of Disinvestment in 2016) works under the Ministry of Finance.

s: The term ‘disinvestment’ was introduced in the Indian policy framework through which of the following?
x: The term ‘disinvestment’ was introduced in the Interim Budget presented in July 1991.

s: Which one of the following was associated with PSU autonomy and Memoranda of Understanding rather than with the disinvestment policy recommendations?
x: Arjun Sengupta’s 1984 work was associated with PSU autonomy and Memoranda of Understanding, not with the later disinvestment recommendations.

s: Up to what share did the Rangarajan Committee (1993) recommend disinvestment in PSUs other than those reserved for the public sector?
x: Rangarajan recommended 49% in reserved PSUs and 74% in others.

s: When was the Department of Disinvestment renamed DIPAM?
x: The Department of Disinvestment (1999) became DIPAM on 14 April 2016.

s: In which year was the Disinvestment Commission set up?
x: The Disinvestment Commission was set up in 1996 with G.V. Ramakrishna as its first chairman.

s: Who headed the early committee on disinvestment set up in 1991?
x: The V. Krishnamurthy Committee (1991) set the early approach; Rangarajan came in 1993.

s: When was the Department of Disinvestment set up?
x: The Department of Disinvestment was set up on 10 December 1999 and renamed DIPAM on 14 April 2016.

s: Of the disinvestment proceeds credited to the National Investment Fund, what is used?
o: Only the income generated from the fund
The entire corpus in the year of receipt
Half of the corpus every year
The corpus, but not the income
x: Disinvestment proceeds go into the NIF, but only the income generated from it is used.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the National Investment Fund?
o: It was set up on 3 November 2005
It is in the Public Account
It was set up in 1995-96 as RIDF
x: NIF (2005) is not RIDF (1995-96).

s: Since which financial year has there been no separate disinvestment head in the Budget, with disinvestment receipts merged into Miscellaneous Capital Receipts?
x: Since FY24, there has been no separate disinvestment head; it has been merged into Miscellaneous Capital Receipts.

s: How many PSUs were covered in the first disinvestment of 1991-92?
x: The first disinvestment in 1991-92 had a Rs 2,500 crore target across 31 PSUs.

s: What is the disinvestment target for 2026-27?
x: The 2026-27 target is Rs 80,000 crore; 2025-26 was Rs 47,000 crore.

s: Against a target of ₹2,500 crore, how much was realised from disinvestment in 1991-92, the first year?
x: In 1991-92 disinvestment in 31 PSUs yielded ₹3,038 crore, more than the ₹2,500 crore target.

s:
Consider the following statements about the National Investment Fund (NIF):
1. It is professionally managed.
2. It is classified under the Public Account.
3. It was created in 1995-96.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
x: The NIF is professionally managed and sits in the Public Account; it was set up in 2005, not 1995-96 (that is RIDF).

s: Which Act was replaced by the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 in relation to the earlier sick-industrial-company regime?
x: The IBC, 2016 replaced the SICA regime, which had been associated with the functioning of BIFR.

s: In which year was the MRTP Act enacted?
x: The MRTP Act was enacted in 1969 and came into force in 1970.

s:
Arrange the following Acts in chronological order:
1. FEMA
2. SICA
3. FERA
4. Competition Act
x: FERA 1973, SICA 1985, FEMA 1999, Competition Act 2002.

s: What did the Industries (Development and Regulation) Act, 1951 provide for?
o: Licensing of new or expanded industrial units and Development Councils
Control of monopolies and restrictive trade practices
x: The IDRA, 1951 provided for licensing of industrial units when started or expanded, and for Development Councils.

s: According to the Hazari Report (1967) and the Dutt Committee (1969), whom had industrial licensing favoured?
x: Both found that the licensing system favoured large business houses, which led to the MRTP framework.

s: In which year was leather removed from compulsory industrial licensing?
x: Leather was delicensed in 1993. Today only four industries need a licence: cigars and cigarettes, electronic aerospace and defence equipment, industrial explosives and hazardous chemicals (DPIIT 2019).

s: Which committee recommended the MRTP Act, 1969?
x: The Dutt Committee, formally the Industrial Licensing Policy Inquiry Committee, recommended the MRTP legislation.

s: After 1991, the role of the Andhra Pradesh Industrial Infrastructure Corporation (APIIC) shifted to which of the following?
x: After 1991, APIIC's role shifted towards being a facilitator of industrial development.

s: In which year was the Industries (Development and Regulation) Act, 1951 amended?
x: IDRA 1951 was amended in 1953.

s: What was the effect of the New Industrial Policy, 1991 on the MRTP asset threshold of Rs. 100 crore?
o: It made the threshold applicable only to public sector firms
It reduced the threshold to Rs. 50 crore
It doubled the threshold to Rs. 200 crore
It scrapped the threshold for large firms
x: The New Industrial Policy, 1991 scrapped the MRTP asset threshold. Large firms no longer required prior approval for expansion, mergers or takeovers merely because of their asset size.

s: Which one of the following was the principal purpose of the Monopolies and Restrictive Trade Practices Act, 1969?
o: To control private monopolies and concentration of economic power
To promote foreign direct investment in high-priority industries
To provide automatic approval for technology agreements
x: The MRTP Act, 1969 aimed to control private monopolies and prevent concentration of economic power. Its enactment followed the recommendations associated with the Dutt Committee.

s: Under the 1984-85 amendment, to what level was the MRTP asset threshold raised?
x: The 1984-85 change set the share at 25% and assets at Rs 100 crore; originally Rs 20 crore.

s: Under the original MRTP Act, 1969, an undertaking was covered if its assets were at least how much?
x: Originally MRTP covered firms with assets of ₹20 crore+ or a 33% market share; it was raised to ₹100 crore in 1984-85.

s: How does asset monetisation differ from disinvestment?
o: Asset monetisation permanently sells equity; disinvestment leases assets temporarily
Both permanently transfer ownership to private operators
Asset monetisation leases public assets for a fixed period with ownership retained by the government; disinvestment permanently sells equity
Both lease public assets for a fixed period without any sale of equity
x: Asset monetisation leases existing public assets for a fixed period after which they return to the government, whereas disinvestment is a permanent sale of equity.

s: With the monetisation of which assets is the National Land Monetisation Corporation (NLMC) associated?
o: foreign exchange reserves held by the Government of India
surplus land and buildings of Central Public Sector Enterprises, including loss-making enterprises
only privately owned industrial land acquired by the government
only the shares of listed Central Public Sector Enterprises
x: NLMC monetises surplus land and buildings belonging to Central Public Sector Enterprises, including those that are loss-making.

s: Which of the following pairs of ports is associated with public-private partnership in Andhra Pradesh?
x: Krishnapatnam and Gangavaram ports are identified as examples of PPP ports in Andhra Pradesh.

s: What is the size of the National Monetisation Pipeline 2.0, launched on 23 February 2026?
x: NMP 2.0 is worth Rs 16.72 lakh crore for FY26-30; NMP 1.0 was Rs 6 lakh crore.

s: Which of the following is the objective of asset monetisation?
o: To unlock the value of existing public assets through new financial structures
To sell majority equity of CPSEs to private buyers
To raise taxes on brownfield assets
x: Asset monetisation leases brownfield assets to unlock their value; ownership stays with the government.

s: What was the size of the National Monetisation Pipeline 1.0 launched in August 2021?
x: NMP 1.0 (August 2021) was worth ₹6 lakh crore for FY22-25.

s: Under which department does the National Land Monetisation Corporation (NLMC) function?
x: NLMC (3 June 2022) works under DPE and monetises surplus land of CPSEs.

s: When was the Board for Industrial and Financial Reconstruction (BIFR) dissolved?
x: BIFR, created under SICA 1985, was dissolved on 1 December 2016 and its cases went to NCLT/NCLAT.

s: Who headed the Bankruptcy Law Reforms Committee that led to the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016?
x: The IBC was enacted on 28 May 2016 after the T.K. Viswanathan-led BLRC (2015).

s: How many sectors does the New PSE Policy, 2021 classify as strategic?
x: There are four strategic sectors (including banking, insurance and financial services), each retaining a bare minimum of 1-4 CPSEs.

s: What was the National Renewal Fund, established in 1992, primarily intended to provide?
o: A safety net and voluntary retirement support for workers affected by restructuring
Foreign exchange support to export-oriented industries
Direct loans to State electricity regulators
x: The National Renewal Fund provided a safety net, including VRS support, for workers affected by industrial restructuring.

s: Under the New PSE Policy 2021, how many CPSEs at most are kept in each strategic sector?
x: The policy keeps 1-4 CPSEs in each of 4 strategic sectors.

s: When was the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code enacted?
x: IBC was enacted on 28 May 2016; NCLT was set up on 1 June 2016.

s: Under which section of the Companies Act, 2013 was the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) set up?
x: NCLT was set up under Section 408 (on 1 June 2016); NCLAT under Section 410.

s: According to the Economic Survey 2025-26, to what level may the Government's stake in listed CPSEs be reduced?
x: The Economic Survey 2025-26 says the stake in listed CPSEs may fall to 26%.

s: What was the original Make in India target for additional manufacturing jobs?
x: Make in India aimed at 100 million additional manufacturing jobs, with 12-14 per cent growth and a 16 to 25 per cent share. 143 million is the National Manufacturing Mission target.

s: Which of the following pairs of Make in India pillars is correctly matched?
o: New Infrastructure – FDI in defence and insurance
New Processes – Single window and e-Biz
New Mindset – Corridors and smart cities
x: New Processes cover single window and e-Biz; New Infrastructure covers corridors and smart cities; New Sectors cover FDI areas; New Mindset sees government as facilitator.

s: Make in India 2.0 covers how many priority sectors?
x: Make in India 2.0 covers 27 sectors: 15 manufacturing under DPIIT and 12 services under the Department of Commerce.

s: The original Make in India initiative of September 2014 covered how many sectors?
x: The original Make in India covered 25 sectors; 27 is the Make in India 2.0 count, 14 the PLI sectors and 12 the champion services sectors.

s: Which strategy reflects the central approach of Make in India?
o: Replacing digital services with traditional services
Restricting manufacturing to wholly state-owned enterprises
Attracting foreign direct investment and global firms to manufacture in India
Promoting only domestic consumption without export orientation
x: Attracting FDI and global firms to establish manufacturing in India is the strategy most typical of Make in India.

s: When was Make in India launched?
x: Make in India was launched on 25 September 2014. Digital India came on 1 July 2015, Skill India on 15 July 2015 and Startup India on 16 January 2016.

s: Which is the nodal ministry for Make in India?
x: Make in India is steered by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry.

s: How many champion services sectors are there under Make in India 2.0?
x: Make in India 2.0 has 27 sectors: 15 manufacturing and 12 services; 25 was the original sector count.

s: Under Make in India 2.0, which body handles the 15 manufacturing sectors?
x: The 15 manufacturing sectors are under DPIIT, while the 12 services sectors are under the Department of Commerce.

s: What is the logo of Make in India?
x: The Make in India logo is a lion made of cogwheels.

s: To what level did the National Manufacturing Policy, 2011 aim to raise manufacturing's share of GDP within a decade?
x: NMP 2011 targeted a 25% manufacturing share of GDP within a decade and 100 million jobs.

s: The National Manufacturing Mission announced in Budget 2025-26 aims by 2035 to achieve which combination?
o: Manufacturing share of 20 percent and 100 million jobs
Manufacturing share of 25 percent and 75 million jobs
Manufacturing share of 25 percent and 143 million jobs
Manufacturing share of 30 percent and 100 million jobs
x: The National Manufacturing Mission targets a 25 percent manufacturing share and 143 million jobs by 2035.

s: What is manufacturing's present share of India's GVA?
x: Manufacturing remains about 16.3–17.5 per cent of GVA, below the 25 per cent target, so the strategy has shifted to scale, design and global value chains.

s: India's manufacturing strategy is criticised for missing which target for manufacturing's share of GDP?
x: The target of raising manufacturing to 25 per cent of GDP has been missed, a stated criticism of the strategy.

s: What was the annual manufacturing growth target of the National Manufacturing Policy, 2011?
x: NMP 2011 aimed at 12-14 per cent manufacturing growth along with a 25 per cent GDP share.

s: Which of the following was specifically included as a measure in the National Manufacturing Policy?
o: Replacing industrial training with fiscal incentives
Restricting skill development to metropolitan areas
x: Skilling of rural youth was specifically included among the policy measures.

s: What is a large integrated industrial township with zoned land use, clean technology and social infrastructure called?
x: NIMZs are conceived as large integrated industrial townships with zoned land use, clean technology and social infrastructure.

s: Under the National Manufacturing Policy, 2011, infrastructure development was envisaged primarily on which basis?
x: The National Manufacturing Policy, 2011 provided for infrastructure on a PPP basis. It did not restrict funding to the public sector, foreign grants or cooperatives.

s: In Andhra Pradesh, NIMZs have been proposed in which districts?
x: NIMZs have received in-principle approval in Chittoor and Prakasam districts of Andhra Pradesh.

s: Which NIMZ in Andhra Pradesh received final approval in 2016?
x: Chittoor and Prakasam got in-principle approval in 2013, but only Prakasam got final approval in 2016.

s: Which of the following is NOT a feature of the National Manufacturing Policy, 2011?
o: Incentives limited to the electronics sector alone
A sector-, location- and technology-neutral approach
x: NMP 2011 is sector-neutral, so incentives limited to one sector are not its feature; PPP infrastructure and rural skilling are.

s: On how many pillars is NITI Aayog's Investment Friendliness Index based?
x: The NITI Index has 8 pillars, B-READY 3 pillars, Doing Business 10 parameters.

s: In NITI Aayog's Investment Friendliness Index (July 2026), Andhra Pradesh was placed in which category?
x: Andhra Pradesh was among the Frontrunners (score 45-50); Gujarat, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, Goa and Odisha were Top Performers.

s: What is District BRAP, or DBRAP, primarily intended to do?
o: Extend business reforms to district-level administration and Tier-II and Tier-III cities
Measure the competitiveness of Indian states against foreign countries
Rank only metropolitan cities on exports
x: DBRAP extends the reform process to districts and Tier-II and Tier-III cities.

s: By whom was the Business Reform Action Plan (BRAP) first released in 2015?
o: DIPP, now DPIIT, in association with the World Bank Group
The Ministry of Finance and the IMF
x: BRAP was first released in 2015 by DIPP, now DPIIT, with the World Bank Group.

s: With which State did Andhra Pradesh share the No. 1 rank in BRAP 2016?
x: Andhra Pradesh was jointly first with Telangana in BRAP 2016 and has been described as No. 1 consistently since.

s: What were the four principles associated with the 435 reform points in BRAP 2024?
x: The BRAP 2024 reform points were organised around Simplification, Elimination, Digitisation and Decriminalisation.

s: When was the AP Single Desk Portal launched?
x: The AP Single Desk Portal was launched in April 2015.

s: Where is the Asian Competitiveness Institute, which ranks Indian States on ease of doing business, based?
x: The ACI is in Singapore and ranks States on three 'ABC' pillars.

s: In BRAP 2019 (released September 2020), which State ranked second?
x: In BRAP 2019, AP was 1st, Uttar Pradesh 2nd (up from 12th) and Telangana 3rd.

s: How many States were Top Achievers in BRAP 2020?
x: BRAP 2020 had no numeric ranks; 7 States, including AP, were Top Achievers.

s: What is the full form of BRAP?
x: BRAP is the Business Reform Action Plan, under which DPIIT ranks States on ease of doing business.

s: Which State ranked first in BRAP 2019, released on 5 September 2020?
x: In BRAP 2019, Andhra Pradesh was first, Uttar Pradesh second and Telangana third.

s: Which State was ranked first in the first BRAP ranking of 2015?
x: BRAP 2015 placed Gujarat first and Andhra Pradesh second.

s: What was Andhra Pradesh's rank in the Asian Competitiveness Institute's Ease of Doing Business Index of 2016?
x: AP was 5th in the ACI index of 2016 and rose to 1st in 2018.

s: On which three pillars does the Asian Competitiveness Institute rank Indian States on ease of doing business?
o: Attractiveness to investors, Business friendliness and Competitiveness policies
Access to credit, Bureaucracy and Contract enforcement
Attractiveness to tourists, Budget discipline and Corruption control
x: The ACI index uses three 'ABC' pillars: Attractiveness to investors, Business friendliness and Competitiveness policies.

s: Which State ranked first in BRAP 2017?
x: In BRAP 2017 AP was 1st, Telangana 2nd and Haryana 3rd.

s: Which State ranked third in BRAP 2019, released on 5 September 2020?
x: BRAP 2019: AP 1st, UP 2nd, Telangana 3rd.

s: Which of the following is NOT a category used in BRAP 2020?
x: BRAP 2020 used Top Achievers, Achievers, Aspirers and Emerging Business Ecosystems; 'Frontrunners' is a NITI Aayog category.

s: In which district of Andhra Pradesh is the JSW Steel project of the Rayalaseema industrial hub?
x: The Rayalaseema hub includes JSW Steel at Kadapa, Kia and Royal Enfield at Tirupati.

s: Under which body does the India Semiconductor Mission function?
x: ISM operates under the Digital India Corporation of MeitY and supports fabs, OSAT/ATMP units and chip design.

s: How many projects have been approved under the India Semiconductor Mission?
x: ISM has approved 12 projects with about ₹1.64 lakh crore of commitments; capital assistance may go up to 50%.

s: What is the outlay of the Semicon India programme (India Semiconductor Mission) of MeitY, approved in 2021?
x: Semicon India/ISM under MeitY was approved in 2021 with an outlay of Rs 76,000 crore.

s: Which one of the following semiconductor units is NOT correctly matched with its location?
o: Tata Electronics–PSMC wafer fab — Dholera, Gujarat
Tata OSAT (Tata Semiconductor Assembly & Test) — Morigaon (Jagiroad), Assam
x: Kaynes Semicon's OSAT is at Sanand, Gujarat, not Dholera. The Tata–PSMC wafer fab (India's first semiconductor-fab SEZ) is at Dholera, Tata OSAT at Jagiroad in Morigaon, Assam, and Micron's ATMP at Sanand.

s: Where is the Tata OSAT unit approved under the India Semiconductor Mission located?
x: The Tata OSAT unit (₹27,120 crore) is at Jagiroad in Morigaon, Assam; Dholera has the Tata-PSMC wafer fab.

s: Where is Micron's ATMP unit under the India Semiconductor Mission located?
x: Micron's ATMP unit is at Sanand, Gujarat, which also hosts the Kaynes and CG Power OSAT units.

s: Where is India's first semiconductor-fab SEZ?
x: The Tata Electronics-PSMC wafer fab at Dholera, Gujarat is India's first semiconductor-fab SEZ.

s: About what share of mobile phones used in India are made in India?
x: About 99.2 per cent of mobile phones used in India are made in India.

s: India is the second-largest mobile phone producer in the world after which country?
x: India is the second-largest mobile phone producer, after China.

s: Which State has the largest number of projects approved under ISM 1.0?
x: Of the 12 ISM 1.0 projects, Gujarat has 6, Odisha 2, and Assam, UP, Punjab and AP 1 each.

s: Up to what share of project cost does the India Semiconductor Mission give as capital assistance?
x: ISM gives up to 50% capital assistance for fabs, OSAT/ATMP and design.

s: With which company is Tata Electronics setting up the semiconductor wafer fab at Dholera, Gujarat?
x: The Dholera fab is a Tata Electronics-PSMC (Taiwan) project worth ₹91,526 crore.

s: In which State is India's first advanced 3D packaging unit?
x: Of the ISM 1.0 projects, the first advanced 3D packaging unit is in Odisha.

s: What was the value of mobile phone production in India in 2024-25?
x: Mobile output rose from ₹18,900 crore (2014-15) to ₹5.45 lakh crore (2024-25).

s: Which was India's largest export category in 2025?
x: Smartphones became India's largest export category in 2025.

s: What are the three pillars of the World Bank's B-READY framework?
o: Regulatory framework, public services and operational efficiency
x: B-READY rests on regulatory framework, public services and operational efficiency.

s: What was India's rank in the World Bank's Doing Business 2020 report?
x: India rose from 142nd in 2014 to 63rd in DB 2020; the report was discontinued in 2021 over data irregularities.

s: The World Bank's Doing Business rankings were meant mainly to guide which of the following?
x: Per the APPSC-GS 2019 key, the Doing Business rankings mainly guide foreign investors on the ease of doing business in a country. They are not meant for consumers, election bodies or monetary policy.

s: In which year was the World Bank's Doing Business report discontinued?
x: Doing Business was discontinued in 2021 over data irregularities and ethics concerns; DB 2020 was the last edition.

s: Which of the following is NOT one of the 10 Doing Business parameters?
x: Getting electricity, resolving insolvency and protecting minority investors are among the 10 parameters; ease of living is not.

s: What was India's rank in the World Bank's Doing Business 2018 report?
x: India rose to 100 in DB 2018, a jump of 30 places; it was 142 in DB 2015 and 63 in DB 2020.

s: With which institution was the World Bank's Doing Business report conceptualised?
x: Doing Business was published by the World Bank Group and conceptualised with the IFC.

s: B-READY, the successor of Doing Business, rests on how many pillars?
x: B-READY has 3 pillars; Doing Business had 10 parameters and the NITI Investment Friendliness Index has 8 pillars.

s: What was India's rank in the World Bank's Doing Business 2015 report?
x: India was 142nd in DB 2015, 100th in DB 2018 and 63rd in DB 2020.

s: The e-Biz platform was introduced as which of the following?
o: A State-level portal exclusively for environmental clearances
A Mission Mode Project under the National e-Governance Plan for online registration, filing and payments
A World Bank index for measuring business regulations
An investment promotion joint venture between FICCI and CII
x: e-Biz is a Mission Mode Project under NeGP that enables online registration, filing and payment for businesses.

s: When was the Foreign Investment Facilitation portal merged with the National Single Window System?
x: The FIF portal was merged with the NSWS in August 2022.

s: Which areas are identified as weak indicators affecting India's ease of doing business?
x: Contract enforcement and property registration remain major bottlenecks; digital literacy and export promotion are not cited.

s: Which broad outcome do the four labour codes and the proposed central rules seek to promote?
o: Replacement of all state labour laws by municipal laws
Formalisation of labour and consolidation of labour regulations
Restriction of employment to the public sector
x: The four labour codes and the draft central rules are associated with labour-law consolidation and increasing formalisation. They do not eliminate informal employment completely.

s: Of the 355 provisions amended by the Jan Vishwas 2.0 Bill, how many were decriminalised?
x: The Bill (introduced 18 August 2025, passed 2026) amended 355 provisions across 16 Acts and decriminalised 288 of them.

s: The SPICe+ reform was introduced to improve which ease-of-doing-business area?
x: SPICe+ supports starting a business; online building-plan approvals target construction permits, IBC insolvency and GST taxes.

s: What is Invest India, established in 2009?
o: A statutory regulator under the Reserve Bank of India for foreign exchange transactions
A World Bank Group index for ranking investment destinations
A not-for-profit joint venture involving DIPP, FICCI, CII, NASSCOM and the States, serving as the national investment promotion agency
A private company established exclusively by NASSCOM for software exports
x: Invest India was established in 2009 as a not-for-profit joint venture involving DIPP, FICCI, CII, NASSCOM and the States, and serves as the national investment promotion agency.

s: The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 is credited with improving which EoDB area?
x: IBC 2016 is credited with improving resolving insolvency.

s: GST (2017) is credited with improving which EoDB area?
x: GST, faceless assessment and e-filing are credited for paying taxes and a unified market.

s: The Jan Vishwas 2.0 Bill amended provisions of how many Acts?
x: Jan Vishwas 2.0 covered 16 Acts and 355 provisions, of which 288 were decriminalised.

s: Despite the four labour codes, about what share of India's workers remain informal?
x: Over 80 per cent of workers remain informal despite the four labour codes.

s: Which of the following is a reform credited with improving India's Ease of Doing Business?
o: Removal of all foreign ownership restrictions
x: Faceless assessment is a credited EoDB reform; removal of all foreign ownership restrictions, nationalisation and PSU expansion are not EoDB reforms.

s: What was India's rank in the IMD World Competitiveness ranking of 2025?
x: India's IMD Competitiveness rank improved from 43 (2021) to 41 (2025).

s: When was PM GatiShakti launched?
x: PM GatiShakti came in October 2021; the National Logistics Policy followed in September 2022.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: PLI schemes came in 2020. The National Manufacturing Policy was 2011, Make in India September 2014 and the India Semiconductor Mission December 2021.

s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Make in India — Manufacturing and investment hub
Digital India — Digital infrastructure, services and empowerment
x: Skill India aims at skilling youth for jobs, not real-time digital payments. Digital India, Make in India and Startup India are correctly matched with their respective objectives.

s: Which of the following missions was launched first?
x: Make in India came on 25 September 2014, before Digital India (1 July 2015), Skill India (15 July 2015) and Startup India (16 January 2016).

s: Which of the following was launched on 15 July 2015?
x: Skill India was launched on 15 July 2015; Digital India came two weeks earlier on 1 July 2015.

s: When was the National Logistics Policy launched?
x: The National Logistics Policy came in September 2022; October 2021 is PM GatiShakti and December 2021 the India Semiconductor Mission.

s: In which year was the National Policy on Electronics announced?
x: The National Policy on Electronics was announced on 20 February 2019.

s: About how many startups had been recognised under Startup India by August 2026?
x: Recognised startups grew from 502 in 2016 to about 2.47 lakh by August 2026.

s: What is the outlay of the India Semiconductor Mission 2.0 approved on 15 July 2026?
x: ISM 2.0 was approved with ₹1,27,500 crore; ISM 1.0 had ₹76,000 crore.

s: The PLI scheme of 2020 covers how many sectors?
x: The PLI scheme covers 14 sectors with an outlay of ₹1.97 lakh crore.

s: What is the outlay of the Mobile Phone Manufacturing Scheme approved on 15 July 2026?
x: The Mobile Phone Manufacturing Scheme (FY27-FY31) has an outlay of ₹62,500 crore; ISM 2.0 is ₹1,27,500 crore.

s: In the context of Make in India and PLI, what does the expression “China+1” refer to?
o: A bilateral tax treaty between India and China
Diversifying global supply chains by adding India as an alternative manufacturing location
Adding one percentage point to India's GDP growth
Replacing China with one Indian state in all trade
x: “China+1” refers to diversification of global value chains by creating an additional manufacturing base, such as India, alongside China.

s: Which one of the following is NOT a pillar of Atmanirbhar Bharat?
x: The five pillars are Economy, Infrastructure, System, Vibrant Demography and Demand. Privatisation is not listed as one of these pillars.

s: What was the size of the Atmanirbhar Bharat package of May 2020?
x: The May 2020 Atmanirbhar Bharat package was about ₹20 lakh crore, roughly 10 per cent of GDP.

s: India's logistics cost, which PM GatiShakti and the National Logistics Policy aim to cut, was historically about what share of GDP?
x: India's logistics cost was historically 13-14 per cent of GDP, which these policies seek to reduce.

s: Which one of the following is NOT a sector included in the PLI scheme as listed?
x: White goods, solar PV modules and specialty steel are included sectors. Coal mining equipment is not included in the listed PLI sectors.

s: The Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme was designed primarily to provide incentives on which basis?
o: Incremental sales of goods manufactured in India
x: PLI provides incentives linked to incremental sales of goods made in India; in electronics, the incentive is stated as 4–6 per cent.

s: What is the outlay of the PLI scheme for the automobile sector (PLI-Auto)?
x: PLI-Auto has an outlay of ₹25,938 crore and requires at least 50 per cent domestic value addition.

s: What is the outlay of PM E-DRIVE, launched by the Ministry of Heavy Industries in 2024?
x: PM E-DRIVE has an outlay of ₹10,900 crore; ₹11,500 crore was FAME-II, which it succeeded.

s: Under the Mobile Phone Manufacturing Scheme (FY2026-27 to FY2030-31), up to what extra incentive is given for domestic sourcing?
x: The scheme gives 2.25-5% on eligible sales, up to 1.5% extra for domestic sourcing and 3% extra for design and R&D by Indian brands.

s: What minimum domestic value addition does PLI-Auto require?
x: PLI-Auto (₹25,938 crore) requires at least 50 per cent domestic value addition.

s: PM E-DRIVE replaced which scheme?
x: PM E-DRIVE replaced FAME-II (2019-24); PLI-LSEM was replaced by the Mobile Phone Manufacturing Scheme.

s:
Consider the following statements about the PLI scheme:
1. It has an outlay of ₹1.97 lakh crore.
2. Coal mining equipment is one of its sectors.
3. Its incentive is paid on incremental sales of goods made in India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The PLI scheme has ₹1.97 lakh crore and pays on incremental sales; coal mining equipment is not one of its sectors.

s: How many jobs had the PLI schemes created by September 2025?
x: By Sept 2025 PLI brought over ₹2.0 lakh crore investment and 12.60 lakh jobs.

s: Which scheme does the Mobile Phone Manufacturing Scheme (FY2026-27 to FY2030-31) replace?
o: PLI for Large Scale Electronics Manufacturing
x: The ₹62,500 crore Mobile Phone Manufacturing Scheme replaces PLI-LSEM.

s: To what amount was the outlay of the Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme (ECMS) raised in Budget 2026-27?
x: Budget 2026-27 raised ECMS from ₹22,919 crore to ₹40,000 crore.

s: In the proposed framework replacing SEZ rules, what does 'DESH' stand for?
o: Development of Export and Special Hubs
Development of Export and Services Hubs
x: DESH is Development of Enterprise & Service Hubs; it would drop compulsory positive NFE, allow DTA sales and be WTO-compliant.

s: When did the SEZ Act, 2005, along with the SEZ Rules, come into force?
x: The SEZ Act and Rules came into force on 10 February 2006.

s: Under Section 10AA, how is the income-tax exemption on export income of an eligible SEZ unit structured?
o: 100 per cent for five years, 50 per cent for the next five years and 50 per cent of ploughed-back profit for a further five years
50 per cent for five years, 100 per cent for the next five years and nil thereafter
50 per cent for the entire fifteen-year period
100 per cent for ten years followed by 25 per cent for five years
x: Section 10AA provides 100 per cent exemption for the first five years, 50 per cent for the next five years and 50 per cent of ploughed-back profit for another five years.

s: Under the sunset clause, Section 10AA benefits go only to SEZ units operational by which date?
x: Only SEZ units operational by 30 June 2020 get the Section 10AA tax benefits.

s: Under the SEZ Act, 2005, who can set up an SEZ?
o: Central Government, State Government or any person
x: An SEZ can be set up by the Central Government, a State Government or any person, including private, joint or foreign developers.

s: Which institution is the nodal agency for recognition of start-ups under the Startup India framework?
x: The Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) is the nodal agency for Startup India recognition.

s: What does the States' Startup Ranking Framework of DPIIT mainly promote?
o: Allocation of all start-up funds exclusively to one state
Direct ranking of individual start-up founders by personal income
Competitive federalism by assessing state start-up policies and their implementation
Assessment of only the number of unicorns in each district
x: The framework promotes competitive federalism by assessing the policies adopted by states and their implementation for start-up development.

s: When was the National Startup Advisory Council notified?
x: The National Startup Advisory Council was notified on 22 January 2020.

s: On which day is National Startup Day observed?
x: Startup India was launched on 16 January 2016, now National Startup Day.

s: MAARG of Startup India is a national platform for which of the following?
x: MAARG is the national mentorship platform of Startup India under DPIIT.

s: What is the name of the single online platform for all stakeholders of India's start-up ecosystem?
x: Startup India Hub is the single platform; Udyam is MSME registration, Standupmitra is the Stand-Up India portal and MAARG a mentorship platform.

s: In which category was Andhra Pradesh placed in the States' Startup Ranking 2022?
x: Andhra Pradesh was No. 1, a Best Performer, in the States' Startup Ranking 2022.

s: Which initiative of Startup India searches for entrepreneurial talent in Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities?
x: Startup India Yatra is a hunt for entrepreneurial talent in Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The National Startup Advisory Council was notified in January 2020.
2. Startup India Yatra searches for entrepreneurial talent only in metro cities.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The Council was notified on 22 January 2020; the Yatra looks for talent in Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities, not metros.

s:
Match the following:
List-I (Platform/Scheme)
A. MAARG
B. Startup India Hub
C. Startup India Yatra
D. SISFS
List-II (Purpose)
1. Single online platform for all stakeholders
2. Mentorship
3. Talent hunt in Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities
4. Proof-of-concept funding
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: MAARG is the mentorship platform, the Hub is the single online platform, the Yatra hunts talent in smaller cities and SISFS funds proof of concept.

s: Which one of the following correctly gives the nodal ministry and the online portal of the Stand-Up India Scheme?
x: Stand-Up India (5 April 2016) is run by the Ministry of Finance through scheduled commercial bank branches, and its portal is Standupmitra. DPIIT is nodal for Startup India, the Udyam portal is for MSME registration, and NITI Aayog is not the nodal body.

s: What is the range of the loan given under the Stand-Up India Scheme?
x: Stand-Up India loans range from ₹10 lakh to ₹1 crore.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Stand-Up India Scheme:
1. It covers greenfield enterprises only.
2. Each bank branch should have at least one SC/ST and one woman borrower.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Stand-Up India covers only greenfield enterprises, and each branch must support at least one SC/ST and one woman borrower.

s: What is the minimum shareholding of an SC/ST or woman entrepreneur in a non-individual enterprise under Stand-Up India?
x: At least 51 per cent shareholding and controlling stake must be with an SC/ST or woman entrepreneur.

s: In which form is working capital up to ₹10 lakh given under Stand-Up India?
o: An overdraft with a RuPay debit card
x: Working capital up to ₹10 lakh is an overdraft with a RuPay debit card; above that it is a cash credit limit.

s: Besides collateral, by the guarantee of which fund may Stand-Up India loans be secured?
o: Credit Guarantee Fund for Stand-Up India Loans
x: Stand-Up India loans are secured by collateral or a CGFSIL guarantee; CGSS is the start-up guarantee scheme.

s: What is the maximum repayment period of a Stand-Up India loan?
x: Stand-Up India loans are repayable in up to 7 years with a moratorium of up to 18 months.

s: Which institution provides the ₹10,000 crore refinance window for Stand-Up India?
x: SIDBI provides ₹10,000 crore refinance for Stand-Up India and also manages the Fund of Funds for Startups.

s: Up to what amount are micro loans given under PM MUDRA (Tarun Plus)?
x: MUDRA's ceiling is ₹20 lakh under Tarun Plus, while Stand-Up India goes up to ₹1 crore.

s: Up to what share of the project cost does a Stand-Up India loan cover?
x: The Stand-Up India loan covers up to 85% of project cost; the borrower puts in at least 10%.

s: What is the maximum moratorium period allowed on a Stand-Up India loan?
x: Stand-Up India loans are repayable in up to 7 years with a moratorium of up to 18 months.

s: When was the Stand-Up India Scheme launched?
x: Stand-Up India was launched on 5 April 2016.
